newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer Medica share price set.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer Medica share price set.

text.p: Sulzer AG said the price for the registered shares being sold in the Initial Public Offering (IPO) of its Sulzer Medica unit was set at 350 francs per share.
The share price for the bookbuilding period had been set between 300 and 350 francs per registered share and between $20.86 and $24.33 per American Depository Share (ADS).
Trading in Sulzer Medica shares and the depository shares is set to begin on July 14 on the Swiss Exchange and on the New York Stock Exchange, respectively.
Sulzer said the global IPO, which closed on July 11, was oversubcribed by more than 25 times. Sulzer made 2.3 million newly issued registered shares available for the offering.
The 800 million francs being raised by the sale will be used entirely by Sulzer Medical to finance its growth strategy, Sulzer said.

In announcing the plan in January Sulzer said the offering was part of a dual growth strategy for the company's medical and technical sectors. It said the industrial side would focus on internal growth, but Medical needed the ability to make acquisitions.

The shares alloted in the IPO were widely distributed to an international investor base, Sulzer said. It said existing shareholders of the parent company, Sulzer AG, subscribed for 313,000 of the total transaction through an Advance Subscription Offering.
Sulzer further stated that it had granted the underwriters an option to purchase an additional 300,000 registered shares to cover over-allotments.

In announcing the start of bookbuilding in June, Sulzer said that as a result of the offering approximately 24 percent of Sulzer Medica's share capital would be held by the public, with the rest remaining with the parent company.
Sulzer Medica makes orthopedic joints, heart pacemakers, artificial valves and arteries. It had sales of 1.6 billion francs in 1996 and employed 4,557 people.
The offering was underwritten by an international syndicate led by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, as Global coordinator, and SBC Warburg as co-global coordinator. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
